findings.state: Dashboard Today surface (?v4=0 / room_dashboard_v4_off), Queue read, GONE QUIET zone, with a deal silent for 30+ days and a dated next step that is not overdue
findings.current: QUIET_PHRASE = /(stalled|stale|days since|gone quiet|no reply|no activity|drift|dark|silent)/i. Deal Workspace recovery.ts:assessStaleness now emits the 30+ day cause as `No recorded activity for ${days} days` (was `Stalled ${days} days`); this cause is causes[0] (recovery.ts:121), becomes health-snapshot top_pressure.cause (health-snapshot.ts:64), then the Dashboard card subtitle -> CommandObject.copy (snapshot-aggregator.ts:111, command-intelligence.ts:203).
findings.problem: Regression from the language work: the new 30+ day wording no longer matches the quiet detector ('No recorded activity' does not match /no activity/, and there is no 'stalled'/'days since'). The most-stale deals (score 100) now fall into NOW/THIS WEEK instead of GONE QUIET unless their next step is also overdue. The 7–29 day wording ('days since last recorded activity') still matches, so the stalest deals are the only ones dropped. adapters.test.ts:91 still feeds the retired literal 'Stalled 42 days', so the test passes while the real input no longer matches.
findings.governing: ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/00_ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL.md (language work must not change behavior); AUDIT_BRIEF §5 'a renamed label that breaks' behavior
findings.proposed: Extend the pattern to the new wording: const QUIET_PHRASE = /(stalled|stale|days since|gone quiet|no reply|no (?:recorded )?activity|drift|dark|silent)/i; and change adapters.test.ts:91 to use the real recovery output 'No recorded activity for 42 days' (keep the old literal as a second case). Better: carry staleDays as a rankingSignal on the deal risk card in snapshot-aggregator.ts so isQuiet does not depend on display text.

findings.state: Dashboard ranking (all three generations) whenever a Quota Workback plan is saved
findings.current: signal-profile.ts:229-235 reads the quota health summary with camelCase keys: qualityScore, pressureScore, touchesWeek, activeAccounts, qualityBand. snapshot-aggregator.ts passes gtmos_quota_targets through raw (parseJson, no translation). quota-workback/lib/persistence.ts:110-128 writes that key in snake_case (quality_score, quality_band, touches_week, active_accounts) and never writes any pressure score.
findings.problem: Contract mismatch between the writer (Quota Workback) and the reader (Dashboard command engine): quotaPressureScore, quotaQualityScore, quotaQualityBand, quotaTouchesWeek and quotaActiveAccounts are always 0/empty. Every quota-driven ranking boost in scoring.ts and every quota reason/copy line ('the quota plan increases this item's priority', 'Your quota plan needs this done this week.', 'Your plan is ahead of the work logged — log or do more outreach.') is dead code, while the Dashboard copy implies the quota plan feeds the ranking. Pre-existing (the aggregator is unchanged from f6416124), not introduced by the language work, but it makes the newly explicit reason copy describe behavior that never happens.
findings.governing: CLAUDE.md Part I §4.18 Flows out ('targets into Dashboard'); AUDIT_BRIEF §5 (copy that claims something the code does not do)
findings.proposed: In snapshot-aggregator.ts readHealthSummaries, normalise the quota summary before handing it to the engine: { qualityScore: q.quality_score, qualityBand: q.quality_band, touchesWeek: q.touches_week, activeAccounts: q.active_accounts, pressureScore: <derived> } with a regression test that saves a plan via saveOutputs and asserts buildSignalProfile sees non-zero values. OWNER DECISION: there is no defined pressureScore formula; either define one (e.g. from readPaceStanding / coverage gap in quota-workback/lib/coverage.ts) or delete the quotaPressureScore branches and their reason/copy strings so the Dashboard stops implying a quota input it never receives.

A renamed label breaking stored history.
